_comment: EPISODE 3, TAKE A, THIRD ATTEMPT (seed 4828). 4827 fixed the microphone and held the street and the cast; this take changes ONE thing and keeps everything else. THE ONE CHANGE: nobody examines the can. In 4827 the can is upright, label to the lens and correctly tallboy-sized at 1.0s, and from 5.0s on -- once people start examining it -- it is horizontal, lid to the lens, label hidden and about hand-length. Three defects, one cause, and the cause was the shot grammar telling every person to take the can and look at it. The `upright` grammar deletes that instruction, states the orientation and the label per shot, and keeps the lid out of frame. Every reaction in this config is a FACE, never a hand on the can.

product._state_comment: THE SEALED GRAMMAR IS OFF, deliberately. Seeds 4824 and 4827 both ran it -- clause, per-shot restatement, a product reference photo that is itself a sealed can, and on 4827 a scene reference too -- and both rendered the can open. Two takes is enough (SKILL.md 31). The mechanism now is the `upright` grammar keeping the LID OUT OF SHOT, so the can's state is never on screen to be wrong. These two keys are the historic wording and they are back only because the sealed grammar is off; the required 'nobody opens a' clause still has to be written by something, and it is still worth having, because a person opening a can mid-shot is its own defect.
product.opening_extra: and no ring pull is touched

_shots_comment: EIGHT shots, two per person, unchanged from 4827. EVERY REACTION IS FACIAL. There is no 'turns it over', no 'sniffs it', no 'squints at it' aimed at the can, no 'reads the label' -- because each of those is an instruction to lift and rotate the product, and that is the defect this take exists to remove.
